head: b2deeb4fa9ed003c994a989de0521b4efb0afb0d
summary: I built the SL-080 diagnostic tooling without touching src/. It adds tests/window/T005Batch.ps1 (ABBA batches of the unmodified T-005 on D:\, with verdict rules fixed in its header before any run), tests/window/StallStacks.ps1 (unelevated EventPipe trace → Speedscope → UI-thread busy stretch matched on the hook's clock → blockedUnder below a pump/dispatch/hook boundary), a per-run summary line and a trace wiring scoped to one process in WindowCases.ps1, and hook facts, a height refusal and a software-render knob. It also adds a findings record at docs/design/SL-080-move-stall.md. Both scripts have -SelfTest modes (11 and 22 canned fixtures, all passing), and I ran all three plans on real D:\. Height 860 vs 644 came out no-measurable-difference: 5 of 8 pairs, median 1.138, but the batch could only have detected a ratio of 2.13 or more, and the order check fired. Trace came out render-path in 4 of 4 traced runs with no masking: the UI thread is in DUCE+Channel.SyncFlush under HwndTarget.UpdateWindowSettings/UpdateWindowPos, plus time inside SetWindowPos. Render came out gpu-present-side: software was lower in 4 of 4 pairs, median ratio 0.305. The brief's 1,318.5 ms is a second kind of stall, about 1.3 s, on a later move. It came in 6 of 17 Height runs at both heights, and also on C:\.

files.why: Batch driver: Height/Trace/Render ABBA schedules with a warm-up. It stops the batch (exit 1) on no summary line, an ending other than the hook's close, the wrong height or render mode, or a null phase. Verdict rules (primaryMs, sign counts, ratio bands, orderEffect, detectableRatio, tracing-masks, render readings) are in the header, fixed before any run. Also -SelfTest/-Only and -Reread.

Stack reader: installs dotnet-trace 10.0.745401 through eng/dotnet.ps1 and reads the nettrace header (start UTC, sampling ns). It rebuilds UI-thread segments, classifies idle from frames only, and matches the wait by time window. It returns NAMED / RENDER-PATH / SPLIT / CANNOT-READ. Also -SelfTest/-Only.
11 canned timelines: named, pump-only, unresolved, external-frames, sampletype-ignored, render-mixed, render-chain, no-ui-samples, no-match, two-waits, idle-floor.

22 canned batches, including each height verdict, drift, quiet, the stop cases (no line, crashed, null phase, height refused or silently clamped, render mode), a summary built through ConvertTo-T005Summary, each trace verdict and each render verdict.

Start-App and Invoke-TreeRun take an environment passed to the one process through Start-Process -Environment. Adds the FSA_T005_HEIGHT/TRACE/SAMPLE_MS/RENDER/TAG/SUMMARY variables for T-005, plus New-T005Trace, Find-T005Trace and ConvertTo-T005Summary. The summary line is written before T-005's checks. FSA_HOOK_RENDER is added to $HookVariables.

Adds a facts line in GAP mode (OS UI thread id through Thread.CurrentOSThreadId, priority class, runtime, render mode and tier, pid, clock origin in UTC and since process start). Each phase's longest wait gains maxEndAt. FSA_HOOK_HEIGHT now refuses a height within the work area that the window does not take.
Adds ClockOriginUtc. FSA_HOOK_RENDER=software sets RenderOptions.ProcessRenderMode=SoftwareOnly before Main.

Findings record: verdict tables, stacks, what this rules in and out against SL-044, programmatic moves vs a user drag, one fix candidate, the FSA_HOOK_MSGLOG contract (not built), and build-time measurements and deviations.

Removed the design-stage SL-080 must_not_import rule, most of whose entries could never fire (review m4). Extended SL-033's 'the shipped app carries no test seam' rule to FSA_HOOK_, FSA_T005_ and tests[\\/]window over src/**.

obligations.how: StallStacks returns CANNOT-READ when more than 20% of the matched stretch names nothing below the pump (unresolved frames, or no managed caller). Fixtures external-frames (80%) and unresolved (70% '?!?') pass. Live: the first traced run was the gate, and on the traced primary stretches at most 1.5% was unreadable.

T005Batch Trace rule: tracing-masks when untraced runs stall in 3 or more of 4 and traced runs in 1 or fewer. Next step is -SampleMs 10, then the fallback. Fixtures trace-masks and trace-masks-10ms pass. Live trace-1: traced 4/4 (median 700.4 ms) and untraced 4/4 (654.1 ms), so no masking.
NAMED needs 3 or more stalling traced runs sharing one blockedUnder; otherwise the verdict is SPLIT. Fixture trace-split (X, Y, Z, X) gives SPLIT; trace-named gives NAMED.

ABBA pairs plus a symmetric orderEffect flag. Fixture height-drift (primary rising 40 ms per run whatever the arm) gives no-measurable-difference with orderEffect true, not 860-worsens. Live height-1 also flagged an order effect: the first run was higher in only 1 of 8 pairs.
no-stall-this-batch when fewer than 4 of 16 runs reach 250 ms, with next = run again. Fixture height-quiet passes.

The hook refuses 'height not applied (asked/actual)'. The driver also stops on any actualHeight that differs from the arm, or on a hook error. Fixtures stop-height-refused and stop-height-silent pass. Live: T005Batch -Plan Height -LowHeight 620 stopped at run 2 with 'height not applied (620/644)', exit 1.

ConvertTo-T005Summary writes a phase the hook never sampled as reached=false with null figures, and primaryMs as null. Fixture summary-phase-never-reached feeds a hook log through the real WindowCases.ps1 function, asserts the nulls, and the batch stops. stop-null-phase also passes.
Invoke-Batch stops with exit 1 at the run that wrote no line, or whose exitReason is not 'closed', and attempts no later run. Fixtures stop-no-line and stop-crashed pass.

StallStacks returns RENDER-PATH, not NAMED, when the chain reaches CompleteRender/SyncFlush or half the stretch is in them. The batch verdict render-path points to -Plan Render. Fixtures render-chain, render-mixed and trace-render pass. Live: all 4 traced runs were RENDER-PATH, so I built and ran the Render plan.

There is one primary metric, primaryMs = max(scan, rescan) longestWaitMs, in the summary line and the T005Batch rules. Other phases are reported but never decided on. A null scan or rescan phase stops the batch (exit 1).

StallStacks has a fixed $Boundary list: the pump, dispatcher plumbing, window procedure, ExecutionContext and ^fsawindowhook! frames, so the hook's Ui()/move lambdas are included. blockedUnder is chosen only below the deepest boundary frame. When nothing covers 90%, the verdict is SPLIT('only the pump is common'). Fixture pump-only passes.

I dropped the collect-mode fallback. The FSA_HOOK_MSGLOG contract (HwndSource hook plus Dispatcher.Hooks, JSON lines per message or operation overlapping [maxAt, maxEndAt]) and the CANNOT-READ reasons that trigger it are in docs/design/SL-080-move-stall.md. It is not built, because no batch read cannot-read or masked.

The Render rule and its readings are in the T005Batch header before any run: gpu-present-side, render-thread-or-dwm-not-gpu (the 'software stalls equally' reading), software-slower, and inconclusive. Arms are interleaved S,H,H,S x2. Fixtures render-gpu, render-equal and render-slower pass. Live render-1: gpu-present-side, median 0.305.

The runtime (.NET 10.0.12) is in the facts line and the summary. The sampling knob is FSA_T005_SAMPLE_MS, which sets DOTNET_EventPipeThreadSamplingRate. Runtime 10.0.12 reads it as hex milliseconds, measured: 'A' gave 10.1 ms spacing and '5' gave 5.1 ms. On tracing-masks the next step is -SampleMs 10. StallStacks classifies idle and busy from frames only and drops CPU_TIME/UNMANAGED_CODE_TIME; fixture sampletype-ignored passes.

The traced exe is launched with Start-Process -Environment carrying the DOTNET_EventPipe* entries, so the script's $env: is never touched. The output path is t005-<run>-{pid}.nettrace, and the runtime substituted the pid in every run.
Test-RunLine stops the batch on exitReason other than 'closed' (timeout, hook error, no close, non-zero exit) and on a null scan or rescan phase. Fixture stop-crashed passes.

The hook logs clockOriginUtc and clockOriginSinceProcessStartMs, and each longest wait gets maxEndAt. StallStacks reads the trace's start UTC from the nettrace header and matches on the time window first, with duration only as a check (busy for 80% or more of the wait). Fixture two-waits (1,018.7 and 809.7 ms) passes. Live offsets were 39.3 to 50.5 ms, and each wait was busy for all but at most 0.6 ms.

I removed the SL-080 must_not_import entry from .taad/fitness.yaml. I extended SL-033's rule over src/** to FSA_HOOK_ and FSA_T005_ (was FSA_HOOK_(MODE|LOG)) and to tests[\\/]window, which also covers csproj files under src/**. src has no match. eng/rules-parity.ps1 printed AGREE.

I reused FSA_HOOK_HEIGHT (TreeMode.Size). $DefaultHeight only feeds T-001's assertions. MinHeight has been 644 since SL-047 (8c47eb7), so 620 cannot be had and the low arm is 644. The only new parts are the refusal and the facts reporting. All of this is recorded in the doc.

verdict.json reports logRatioSd and detectableRatio, computed as exp((t0.975 + t0.80) * sd / sqrt(n)). The doc quotes 2.13 next to the no-measurable-difference verdict and says it is not 'does not worsen it'.
Both scripts have -SelfTest with -Only, fed by canned files. StallStacks passes 11 of 11 and T005Batch passes 22 of 22. -Only with an unknown name exits 1.

The doc has a section 'Programmatic moves, and a person's drag'. The stacks come from the hook's SetWindowPos through the dispatcher, not DefWindowProc's modal loop. The render-side SyncFlush wait is expected to carry over to a drag, but the part inside SetWindowPos is the hook's own, and no drag was traced.

deviations: The low arm is 644 px, not 620. At HEAD, MinHeight is 644 (SL-047, 8c47eb7), so a 620 window cannot be had; the design assumed 620 was reachable. Measured live: T005Batch -Plan Height -LowHeight 620 stopped at run 2 with the hook's 'height not applied (620/644)'.

The sampling option is FSA_T005_SAMPLE_MS, not FSA_T005_SAMPLE_NS. Runtime 10.0.12 reads DOTNET_EventPipeThreadSamplingRate as hexadecimal milliseconds. Measured: 'A' gave 10.1 ms between samples, '5' gave 5.1 ms, '2710' held the app's exit 7.5 s, and '989680' hung it. A nanosecond value would have hung the app.

StallStacks' idle floor is 25%, not 60%. The first traced T-005 run was idle 49.4%, with every idle sample in Dispatcher.GetMessage, because the hook's moves hold the UI thread in SyncFlush for about half the run. At 60% every real run would have read CANNOT-READ.

Stretch matching is by time window, and the only duration check is that the stretch is busy for 80% or more of the wait. The design's duration match within 20% would miss a stretch the probe was let through in the middle of: in the first run the scan's stretch was 201 ms around an 83 ms wait. A stretch half or more in the render flush reads RENDER-PATH before SPLIT is considered, because the rescan stretches have only the pump in common at 90% yet are 51 to 77% SyncFlush.

The hook refuses a height only within the work area. T-003 asks 4000 and relies on the clamp to the work area. A refusal of every clamped height would have broken T-003, which passed after the change.
uiThread comes from Thread.CurrentOSThreadId by reflection. AppDomain.GetCurrentThreadId returns the managed id on .NET (it gave 2), and a P/Invoke is ruled out by InteropLivesOnlyInNative (tests).

I built the conditional render arm (FSA_HOOK_RENDER) after the first traced gate run read RENDER-PATH, before the Trace batch confirmed it. The Trace batch then read render-path in 4 of 4 runs, and the Render plan ran as the design says.

T005Batch has a -Reread switch, not in the design. The first Trace batch's reader failed after all 9 runs because the script-level $Stacks path was shadowed by Invoke-Plan's $stacks table. After the fix, the same rules re-read the same runs.jsonl and traces (trace-1) rather than re-running T-005.
not_built: FSA_HOOK_MSGLOG, the in-process fallback. Its contract is in docs/design/SL-080-move-stall.md, but no batch reached cannot-read or tracing-masks, which are its triggers.
A scan of the real contents of D:\. The design read 'real D:\' as T-005's tree placed on D:\, and the design-slice open question on this is still for a person.

Any elevated ETW/WPR capture of the render thread or DWM. EventPipe cannot see the render thread, and the engine's admin list (whoami, read-denied-folders) has no trace operation. The design-slice open question on authorising it is still for a person.
A Trace re-run at -SampleMs 10. It was not needed, because tracing did not mask the stall (traced 4/4, untraced 4/4).
follow_ups: Fix candidate from the findings: draw the main window in software at scan start (HwndTarget.RenderMode = SoftwareOnly, or process-wide), A/B it with T005Batch's rules, and price what software drawing costs the 100,000-row tree. The measured lower bound here is 169 to 344 ms instead of 507 to 685 ms, still over 250 ms in 1 of 4 runs.

Trace the ~1.3 s kind on its own. It came in 6 of 17 Height runs at both heights, 1 of 9 Trace runs and 0 of 9 Render runs, and in a plain T-005 on C:\ (1,352.6 ms). It was traced once (run 4): 92% under HwndTarget.UpdateWindowPos > UpdateWindowSettings > SyncFlush.

T-005 intermittently fails its own 1 s bar through the ~1.3 s kind (the plain run at the end of this build failed at 1,352.6 ms). A person should decide whether that bar stays as it is while the stall is unfixed.
D:\fsa-sl080-temp was left in place: it is the temp folder this build created for the batches, and the engine blocked its removal as a protected path. Its case folders are removed by T-005 itself.
idleGapS is about 0 in every run because the runs are back to back. If idle time before a run matters (spike stall-follows-run-order-not-build never ran), a schedule with pauses would be needed.

tests.command: pwsh -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File eng\dotnet.ps1 build tests\window\FsaWindowHook\FsaWindowHook.csproj -c Release -o artifacts\window-hook
tests.note: 0 warnings, 0 errors, after each hook change.
11 of 11 fixtures. The first attempts failed: a fixture-generator bug (a one-element mix unrolled) and a self-test exit plumbing bug, both fixed.

22 of 22 fixtures. On an earlier run, height-no-difference had an order effect built into its data by mistake (fixture fixed, not the code), and summary-phase-never-reached first had the wrong arm height.
Exits 1 with 'no fixture named', so a filter that matches nothing is never a pass.

tests.command: pwsh -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File tests\window\WindowCases.ps1 -Case T-005 (TEMP/TMP=D:\fsa-sl080-temp, FSA_T005_SUMMARY/TRACE/HEIGHT=860/TAG set)
tests.note: Gate traced run: rescan wait 489.6 ms, 10.4 MB nettrace. The reader's first readings failed (60% idle floor, a clock parse that lost ms, uiThread 2 = the managed id), all fixed. It then read RENDER-PATH: 77% SyncFlush, the wait matched to its stretch at a +204.4 ms offset.

Real D:\, 17 runs. Verdict no-measurable-difference: 860 higher in 5 of 8 pairs, median 1.138, logRatioSd 0.656, detectableRatio 2.13, orderEffect true (first higher in 1 of 8). 16 of 16 runs stalled.
All 9 runs completed, but the stack reader crashed on every traced run ($Stacks shadowed by a local table), so the verdict came out cannot-read. Bug fixed; see the -Reread entry.

Verdict render-path: 4 of 4 traced runs RENDER-PATH, traced stalls 4/4 vs untraced 4/4, so no masking. Rescan first move: 51-55% SyncFlush plus 43-47% inside SetWindowPos. Run 4's 1,367 ms: 92% HwndTargetFilterMessage > HandleMessage > UpdateWindowPos > UpdateWindowSettings > SyncFlush.
Verdict gpu-present-side: software lower in 4 of 4 pairs, median ratio 0.305 (software 169-344 ms, hardware 507-685 ms), hardware stalls 4/4.
Expected stop: exit 1 at run 2, 'hook-error: height not applied (620/644)'. The warm-up and run 1 at 860 ran; the warm-up stalled 1,415 ms.
The FSA_HOOK_HEIGHT=4000 clamp path is not refused. Opens took 121.6 ms cold and about 3 ms warm.
Plain run: no SL-080 variables, tree in %TEMP% on C:\. It failed T-005's own 1 s bar: scan max 1,352.6 ms (the ~1.3 s kind this slice measures). Every other check held.
Start-App's default path, without an environment, is unchanged.
Tree mode without GAP or a height is unchanged.
AGREE: 12 facts, 16 twinned entries, 29 patterns, 46 settled entries.

tests.command: pwsh -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File eng\dotnet.ps1 build FsAnalyser.slnx -c Release
each case command: pwsh -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File tests\window\<StallStacks|T005Batch>.ps1 -SelfTest -Only <fixture> (13 fixtures, incl. the 9 case commands)
